title: Virtual environments and pip
summary: Isolated installs per project, and pinned dependencies.

steps.title: Why virtual environments
body: In .NET each project lists its NuGet packages and restores them per project. Python installs packages **into an interpreter**. Without care, every project on your machine shares one set of packages, and upgrading one breaks another.
A **virtual environment** (venv) is a private copy of the interpreter's package folder for one project:
python -m venv .venv            # create it (once per project)
.venv\Scripts\activate          # Windows: use it in this shell
python -m pip install requests  # now installs into .venv only
Add `.venv/` to `.gitignore`: it is rebuilt from the requirements, never committed (like `bin/` and `obj/`).

steps.prompt: Arrange the steps to start working on a freshly cloned project.
You run `pip install pandas` with no venv active, and another project's code now breaks. Why?
options: It installed into the shared interpreter and changed a version the other project relied on
The other project needs to be recompiled
steps.explain: Without a venv, all projects share one site-packages folder. One venv per project keeps their dependencies apart.

steps.title: pip and requirements
body: `pip` is the package installer (NuGet's `dotnet add package`). Packages come from **PyPI**.
python -m pip install requests==2.32.3   # exact version
python -m pip list                       # what is installed
python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt  # pin everything currently installed
A `requirements.txt` is one requirement per line: `requests==2.32.3`. Pinning exact versions makes installs reproducible, like a lock file.
> **Tip:** `python -m pip` guarantees you use the pip of the Python you mean, which avoids "installed it but cannot import it" confusion.

steps.prompt: Match the .NET tool or file to its Python counterpart.
This script reads a requirements file. What does it print?
steps.explain: Comments and blank lines are ignored. Only `==` pins an exact version; `>=` allows upgrades.

steps.prompt: Commit it to git, or not?

steps.title: Requirements checker
prompt: Read a requirements file from input until a line `---`, then lines of installed packages as `name version` until `end`.
For each requirement (in file order, skipping blanks and `#` comments) print one line:
- `ok NAME` if installed and (when pinned with `==`) the version matches
- `wrong NAME: want X, have Y` if pinned and the version differs
Unpinned requirements (just a name) only need to be installed. Names compare case-insensitively.

tests.name: mixed
tests.stdin:
# deps
requests==2.32.3
flask

pytest==8.3.2
---
requests 2.31.0
Flask 3.0.3
end

hints: `partition("==")` gives the name and version (empty when unpinned).
Keep installed packages in a dict keyed by lowercase name.
